grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: まちます。まってください。

tables.caption: Polite statement form → taught te-form → request ending. Every whole pair is translated in the note.
Already known polite verb past and negative-past patterns, with new meanings translated in the note.

grammar.note_en:
A request asks another person to act. The speaker’s polite statement まちます means “I wait/will wait”; まってください means “please wait.” The request uses a taught te-form plus ください, not the polite ます form plus ください. These twelve complete changes are the bounded inventory here. Learn the actual whole pair rather than guessing by replacing ます with て. まちます → まってください = “please wait”; とります → とってください = “please take”; てつだいます → てつだってください = “please help with a task”; はこびます → はこんでください = “please carry”; たすけます → たすけてください = “please help/rescue someone in difficulty”; おさえます → おさえてください = “please hold steady”; みます → みてください = “please look”; おきます → おいてください = “please put down”; しめます → しめてください = “please close”; よみます → よんでください = “please read”; かきます → かいてください = “please write”; のみます → のんでください = “please drink”.

てつだいます means helping someone with a task; たすけます focuses on helping someone in immediate difficulty. Mei’s occupied hands and the opening cupboard make たすけてください a real request for assistance. おさえます means holding something steady; it does not mean opening it. Waiting, holding the door and taking a bowl are separate jobs, and every handover is stated before the first person lets go.

ちゃわん here is a small ceramic tea/drinking bowl without a handle; さら is a plate and おぼん a tray. て is the body-part noun “hand”; the identical sound at the end of まって is not another hand. われます describes a brittle bowl breaking. われましたか asks “did it break?” and われませんでした says “it did not break.” ぬれます means get wet; ぬれました reports that it got wet, while ぬれませんでした reports that it did not. Those are the already-known polite verb past/negative patterns applied to these new verbs, not adjective negatives or adjective pasts.

A つつみ is a wrapped bundle, ひも the cord around it, and ふう the seal closing it. A しみ is a stain; 水のしみ in the story is a water stain. None of these words identifies the package, its contents or its owner. The team moves the intact bundle, not its contents. Plain verb forms, negative requests, te-form clause chains and ongoing/result ています are not taught here. ゆっくり means slowly; it modifies the action without a new ending.

Known place/destination/source patterns are reused with concrete hands and surfaces: みぎのてにちゃわんがあります = “there is a tea bowl in the right hand”; めいのてからちゃわんをとります = “take a bowl from Mei’s hand”; つくえへはこびます = “carry it to the table.” They do not license a new general body-position paradigm.

The programme is recopied on a separate large sheet for TODAY’S evening event, with the same four named turns. The old shop-price memo remains intact; the two original staff cards and four later public invitations are separate objects. First-parcel books begin on their established external shelf, not inside the cupboard. Known-word spellings add 持・読・書・飲・水・茶 only, with complete source-bound kana readings. Newly introduced nouns and verbs remain kana, including て and ふう.

notes: Original contemporary Japanese narrative, invented present-day programme titles, exercises and four vector diagrams. No private-letter, sealed-bundle, second-parcel or archive contents are quoted. No audio is assumed.

Four developed scenes turn an opening-cupboard collision risk into coordinated jobs, then protect shelf books, enlarge the agreed programme and respond to an unexplained wet wrapper. The first parcel’s books never originate inside the cupboard. All bowl/door/box/document/bundle transfers are explicit.

The formal programme is tonight/day6/16th. It retains Yui/picturebook → Ren/newspaper → Mei/story → Haru/song; its new large sheet is separate from the financial memo, four public copies and two original staff cards. Both story and song titles are clarified. Haru is an adult retired sign painter, not portrayed as unable to read normal lettering.

Eighteen new semantic units = nine reserved plus nine selected open slots, below the21 ceiling; existing stable put/use meanings retain their earlier introductions. Six new characters 持読書飲水茶 spell known words only. New learner meanings remain kana; exact-source authored spans cover all story Han.

Every scene has two five-response drills; Pensa adds8A+8B+6C,62 responses total. Models perform the actual task, noun/verb banks have three same-class extras, and C gives visible story-stage restrictions. The88% part2 prior-coverage advisory is unchanged.

The unknown sealed bundle moves intact onto protective ordinary paper on the small table beside the cupboard; its wrapper/seal and the protective sheet show water. The books/programme remain dry, cups stay in the separate small tea room, Haru’s red borrowed tools remain due tonight, and the blue paid repair parts remain distinct.

JA11-Q2 [?] Check all new meanings and three meaningful lexical uses, especially hand て versus verb endings and seal ふう versus ふうとう. Inspect genuine first-match card contexts and authored reading spans rather than substring counts.

JA11-Q3 [?] Assess substantial four-scene volume, the clearer two-title programme, room/shelf/table custody, intact unidentified bundle/wet-dry contrast, the outstanding tool loan and all62 task-specific keys/models. Retain the measured88% coverage advisory for independent judgment.

Whole-unit scanning finds at least3 uses per new meaning; hand is7 genuine noun uses rather than the analyser’s overlapping suffix count.
